### What Wave A says

1. **The filter is the larger effect, and it carries over to the open
   population.** On its own it takes 36–39% off T @ 4,000, mostly through mix
   (it stops dispatching vehicles that cannot finish, which are mostly
   xavier) plus a ~13-point waste channel.
2. **The score still adds value on top of the filter in the open
   population**, the method's main claim: gpu+F is a further 9–15% faster
   than baseline+F in every seed. The combination is **sub-additive**. Both
   parts remove xavier dispatches, so the combined −44 to −45% falls short of
   even the multiplicative −48 to −51%.
3. **Under persistent identity (closed), the antagonism survives the open
   trace timing:** gpu+F is slower than baseline+F in every seed (+3.9 to
   +11.2%). The G_i divergence, amplified by the filter (xavier : thor up to
   4.5×), is the visible mechanism. **In the closed pool, the filter alone is
   the best configuration.**
4. **The spec beats observation with the filter on as well** (open, −11 to
   −13%), and the fairness cost does not grow with the filter.
